observations: A Rust unit test of the production admission validator accepted the exact receipt and rejected altered or extra fields, lease replay, changed window/document/configuration owner, changed source session identity/target/configuration, parent scope replacement, selector revision drift, family changes, and mode changes.

The lease transfer test verified exact candidate retention until weak destination refs validated, one-use acquisition, source-map teardown, descendant collection, and same-origin open-root/frame traversal.

Empty, replaced, and stale scopes returned no candidates without widening; the root and outside targets were excluded, focus and scroll were preserved, and the existing weak Set scroll-target setter passed.
All 1,000 create/acquire/teardown cycles passed with forced GC enabled; the connected exact weak target remained usable afterward and retained element, observer, and window counts were zero.
The 1,000-cycle scope lifecycle script completed in 1,087 ms in the engine suite and 1,111 ms in the repository-wide check; these are fixture timings, not a production benchmark.
Repository check passed QML lint and UI tests, generated-document and resource checks, release/license checks, formatting, and all workspace Rust tests.
